rows.after: Added a parallel `NpcEncoding` loader matching the InventoryEncoding pattern: `loadNpcEncoding()` (cached, fetched from /data/npc_encoding.json), `lookupNpcByStored(encoding, storedValue)` returning `{iid, speakerNpcId, category, subIndex, jpName, enName}` or null, the `NpcInfo` / `NpcEncoding` types, and a `NPC_CATEGORY_LABELS` map for display ('main NPC' / 'staff / special' / 'guest / event' / 'mythical / creature'). The new helpers handle the stored_value→NPC resolution that the Friends-Met section needs.

rows.before: SlotParse had `townResidents: TownResident[]` but no field for the friend / encounter-list region at body 0x500..0x4300. There was no FriendMet interface.
rows.after: Added a `FriendMet` interface (`storedValue`, `bodyOffsets[]`, `iid`) documenting the dedupe-by-value contract and the open question about sub-region boundaries within 0x500..0x4300 (translation-repo notes/savefile_format.md §55). Added `friendsMet: FriendMet[]` to SlotParse alongside `townResidents`. The interface deliberately stays minimal — name resolution is layered on at render time from the loaded NpcEncoding so the parser bundle doesn't have to embed all 252 names.
rows.reason: Type contract for the new parser path. Mirrors the InventoryBagSlot / TownResident shape (parser produces structural rows; component resolves names) the rest of the editor uses.

rows.before: Parser walked the documented save regions (catalog, mail, garden, inventory bag, town residents, etc.) but had no scan for the 0x500..0x4300 NPC-history region — that region was undecoded.
rows.after: Added `parseFriendsMet(body)` and exported it. The scanner walks body 0x500..0x4300 at EVEN-aligned u16 offsets, collects every value in 500..751 (the NPC stored_value range per translation-repo step-346), groups by value, and returns a list sorted ascending by stored_value. The 'even-aligned only' rule is the load-bearing false-positive filter — odd offsets walk straight through unrelated record boundaries; even-aligned scan on the tongari_en.dsv fixture yields exactly 4 NPCs with zero noise. Added matching OFFSETS constants (`friendsRegionStart`, `friendsRegionEnd`, `friendStoredValueMin`, `friendStoredValueMax`), wired the call into the populated-slot return of parseSlot, added an empty-array fallback to the uninitialised-slot branch, and registered a REGION_DESCRIPTORS.friendsMet entry for the inspector UI.
rows.reason: Core parser logic for the read-only Friends-Met view. Dedupe-by-value is the right shape because the 15 KB region contains several sub-tables (encounter log, friend list, gift log, etc.) that each reference the same NPC, so per-offset noise would obscure the actual roster.

rows.before: Inspector rendered checksum, profile, inventory, residents, catalog, etc. sections but had no Friends-Met UI. The component had no NpcEncoding state and never called loadNpcEncoding().
rows.after: Added a `FriendsMetSection` React component placed directly below the Town Residents section (matches the dispatch-brief layout request). The section renders a 5-column table (stored_value with hex+decimal, EN name, JP name, category label, reference count) with names resolved at render time via lookupNpcByStored(npcEncoding, storedValue). Untouched-but-loading states show 'loading…' instead of fake names; if npcEncoding loaded but ok=false it surfaces a load-failure warning. Threaded a new npcEncoding state through SlotView via a new NpcEncoding prop on SlotViewProps. The component's body copy explicitly explains the distinction between Town Residents (up to 8 NPCs who physically moved into the player's town) and Friends Met (broader roster of every NPC the player has interacted with) so users understand why both panels exist.
rows.reason: User-visible surface for the new parse path. Read-only because sub-region boundaries inside 0x500..0x4300 aren't yet decoded — adding/removing individual friends would require knowing which sub-table to modify to keep the others consistent.

rows.before: Test harness covered wrapper detection, checksum verification, active-slot detection, profile edits, ritch edits, catalog edits, inventory edits, and town-residents parsing. No coverage of the friends-met region.
rows.after: Added a Friends-Met assertion block scoped to the fixture's active slot (B). Loads npc_encoding.json synchronously from disk (mirrors the inventory_encoding pattern), prints each parsed friend with EN/JP name and offsets, then asserts: count = 4 (no false positives, no missed entries), each row's storedValue / iid / EN name / JP name matches, dedupe is real (Chloe@506 has multiple offsets), sort is ascending. The expected roster is `[505→Zoe, 506→Chloe, 507→Silvia, 517→Naomi]` — derived from a standalone even-aligned scan of the fixture bytes. (Dispatch-brief NOTE: the brief named `[505→Zoe, 506→Chloe, 509→Anson, 517→Naomi]` from a different save's offset annotations, but the actual fixture bytes don't contain stored_value 509 anywhere — the third friend is 507=Silvia, not 509=Anson. Asserting against the real fixture state rather than the typo'd reference is the correct call per CLAUDE.md 'never let a bailout clause hide ground truth' — we surface what's actually in the bytes.)
rows.reason: Empirical anchor for the parser path. Without coverage future refactors could silently re-break the friends-met scan exactly like step-262 did with town residents. The fixture's actual contents are the source of truth, not draft notes about a different save.
